title: Climbing
summary: Vocabulary lasts about three minutes. Then somebody suggests you get on the wall, and the suggestion is friendly.

larp.dek: The scene is physical and the grade is public. Your body is the audit and it runs in front of everyone.

crib.heading: References
lines: V-scale for boulder, French or YDS for rope. Know which the room uses.
Fontainebleau, Hueco, Céüse as the named places.
Beta is the sequence. Flash, onsight and project are three different things.
Ondra and Sharma are the household names, which is itself a tell.

crib.heading: Opinions to hold
lines: Grades are soft everywhere except at your own gym.
Indoor and outdoor are different sports.

phrases.line: I'm coming back from a finger thing.
phrases.when: Handed a problem you cannot climb. Universal, unfalsifiable, and it buys you the session.
phrases.invites: Sympathy, and a long conversation about pulleys. Know the word A2.

phrases.line: It's not the grade, it's the reach.
phrases.when: Watching somebody fail a problem. Talking about movement rather than numbers is the tell of a climber.
Asked whether you are getting on the wall. Postponement is normal here.

surface: Vocabulary lasts about three minutes. Then somebody suggests you get on the wall, and the suggestion is friendly.
There is no version of this scene that stays verbal.

follow_up.question: "Want to jump on this one?"
follow_up.why: It is an invitation rather than a test, which is exactly why it is fatal. You can decline once. You cannot decline twice.

counter.move: Say you are coming back from a finger injury, then offer to belay. Every climber has had one, nobody can check it, and belaying keeps you at the wall doing something useful instead of standing next to it.
counter.holds: One session. It does not survive a second invitation, and the gym will remember that you never got on the wall.

tells: Your hands are wrong. Nobody who climbs has those hands.
You know the numbers but not the movement, and you describe routes by grade instead of by what they ask of you.
You say you climb but not where. Every climber has a home wall and names it in the first sentence.
cost: Low socially, high in the moment. Nobody is angry and everybody saw it.
The scene is small enough that the story travels to the next gym before you do.

learn.book: The Rock Warrior's Way — Arno Ilgner
learn.make: Twelve sessions. Nothing substitutes for the sessions.

content.proof_of_work: Your hands and your movement, both visible within seconds of arriving. This is the craft on the list where the equipment gets handed to you unprompted.

tools.name: Shoes
tools.why: Fit and downturn are the first thing anybody asks about, and everyone has a complaint.

tools.name: Chalk
tools.why: Liquid or loose is a real preference and a cheap thing to hold.

tools.name: Brush
tools.why: Cleaning holds is etiquette, and not doing it marks you immediately.

techniques: Flagging, heel hooks and drop knees are the words for what the body is doing.
Beta is the sequence; asking for it is normal and offering it uninvited is not.
Reading a problem from the ground before touching it is the visible part of the skill.
failure_modes: Pulling with the arms because the feet are not being used.
Chasing grades rather than movement, which the room can see.
Finger injuries from volume too early: the A2 pulley is the one everybody names.
